intent: owner rejected the Raft<->MDLP 1:1 isomorphism (different purposes) and redirected to the real idea: teacher/student as ROTATABLE ROLES, peer learning designed from Raft's role machinery

Transfers T1-T8 from Raft (epoch-scoped roles, qualification checked by others not self-asserted, randomized selection doing triple duty, free step-down via no persistent role state, epoch-stamped teaching acts, teach-as-instruction-and-measurement, KRaft observers as the newcomer state, pull-not-push from the substrate argument) and explicitly refuses two (leader-log-is-always-right -> would be transfer poisoning, B3 zero-trust is correct; passive followers -> students must not be passive)
learned: the sharpest result came from where Raft is WRONG for this: Raft's voting rule is argmax-completeness, but peer teaching is unimodal in the competence gap, not monotone - so qualification is a BAND [delta_min, delta_max], which is a computable zone-of-proximal-development and is learnable per skill by the same machinery SS19 uses for gate thresholds. Second: randomized teacher assignment does symmetry-breaking + exploration + causal IDENTIFICATION at once, turning the fleet into a continuously-running randomized trial. Third: teaching produces TWO held-out measurements, so 'does teaching pay the teacher' is a measurable fork - if yes peer learning is self-incentivising and needs no fleet-altruism term at all. Also: I over-generalized in the prior turn and the owner caught it; the useful lesson is that a mechanism-level mapping is not a problem-level identity

intent: dedicated ontology study for MDLP, separate from the Raft material
did: wrote docs/research/STUDY-ontologies-for-mdlp.md. Verified first that knowledge tracing/BKT/IRT are already covered (PAPER, REPORT, ALGORITHM SS3) and ontology/OntoClean/SHACL/SKOS/ESCO/competency-questions appear nowhere in the corpus. Central claim: SS5.1 growth IS an ontology-learning system - maps 1:1 onto the Buitelaar/Cimiano layer cake (terms->synonyms->concepts->taxonomic->non-taxonomic->axioms), MDLP does layers 1-5 and has NO axiom layer, and concepts have intension+extension but no lexicon. Six threads: OntoClean meta-properties to DERIVE constraints instead of discovering them reactively; the granularity blind spot (tau_new has hysteresis but no principle, and over/under-splitting are both invisible to a competence gate); ontology evaluation's 5 families of which MDLP does exactly one (task-based = the held-out gate, unnamed); competency questions as the specifiable definition of 'representative' for G4; portability via stable ids + ESCO/CTDL mappings; and property-graph-not-RDF practicalities (Neo4j GRAPH TYPE's validate-on-write beats SHACL's validate-on-invoke; take semantics not stack). Queues ONT-1-prime and ONT-3..7
learned: the grep before writing changed a conclusion and caught an error in my own prior study: B2 Amendment A ALREADY enforces union-scoped acyclicity at the GraphStore.merge() write path reporting via MergeReport.rejected, for grown AND authored edges - i.e. ONT-1's mechanism is already built and approved. Two consequences: ONT-1 gets cheaper (generalize one hardcoded check to a declared table, not build a gate), and a NEW finding emerged - that single constraint arrived REACTIVELY as a caught gap in a late review round, which is the L-013/C2 reactive-constraint pattern showing up a third time, and OntoClean is exactly the discipline that would derive it proactively. Also found MDLP is AHEAD of the prerequisite-learning field in one unnamed way: decay_edges' intervention-renewal + B2's q_edge quota together are a randomized-intervention policy, i.e. causal support, which the field treats as the gold-standard signal vs co-occurrence baselines
